kept.excerpt: Far from their best, Argentina avoided a huge World Cup upset as they eventually overcame a stubborn Cabo Verde side to reach the last 16. Messi scored his seventh goal of the tournament in the 3-2 victory. FIFA described Argentina's players suffering cramp and fatigue, with Egypt their next opponent.
kept.relevance: The official report establishes Messi's strong individual production and Argentina's continued participation, while documenting a difficult knockout performance and physical strain.

kept.excerpt: Reigning champions Argentina needed an extra-time own goal to clinch a dramatic 3-2 victory over Cape Verde and a place in the last 16. Messi gave Argentina the lead in the 29th minute with his seventh goal of the tournament and delivered the corner that produced the decisive own goal. Reuters reported that, Messi aside, Argentina were largely bereft of ideas against Cape Verde's defence.
kept.publisher: Reuters, syndicated by Sports Radio KWSN
kept.relevance: Independent reporting shows Messi's central role in Argentina's attack and the team's vulnerability, both relevant to his prospects of sustaining an award-winning tournament.

kept.excerpt: Argentina and Egypt were scheduled to meet in the round of 16 in Atlanta at noon on Tuesday, July 7. Argentina reached the fixture by outlasting Cape Verde in extra time. Messi, 39, and Mohamed Salah, 34, had previously met twice in the UEFA Champions League, but this would be their first meeting representing their national teams.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day preview verifies Argentina's immediate elimination hurdle and Messi's age without incorporating the subsequent match result.

kept.excerpt: El Doce reported from Argentina's last open training session before the round-of-16 match against Egypt. Lionel Messi appeared at the session, described as relaxed and happy amid high summer temperatures. The segment aired on Noticiero Doce on July 6, 2026.
kept.relevance: Contemporaneous training coverage provides a recent observable participation update before Argentina's next knockout match.

kept.excerpt: France captain Kylian Mbappé scored twice as France opened its campaign with a 3-1 victory over Senegal. Messi responded with a hat-trick in Argentina's 3-0 win against Algeria. Le Monde reported that the two opening performances attracted international media attention.
kept.relevance: This dated tournament report identifies another prominent individual performer and documents the early attention surrounding Messi's performances.

kept.excerpt: Lionel Messi became the first man to win the World Cup Golden Ball twice. After winning the award at Brazil 2014, he received it again at Qatar 2022 after providing seven goals and three assists. Mbappé and Luka Modrić received the Silver Ball and Bronze Ball respectively.
kept.relevance: This establishes Messi's exceptional historical award record and supplies a prior winning performance benchmark for evaluating his 2026 candidacy.

search_notes: Frozen evidence pack for Q063 with publication cutoff 2026-07-06 inclusive. Publication dates were checked against article datelines, extracted publication metadata, or the video's explicit publication and broadcast date. The Reuters syndication displays July 3 at 8:16 PM local time; extracted metadata gives the equivalent July 4 at 01:16:56 UTC. Searches surfaced later material, which was excluded; no subsequent match results or award outcome are included. Dynamic related-story modules and navigation were excluded from evidence. An AFA report about Messi's player-of-the-match awards was dropped because a verifiable publication date was unavailable. No betting pages, prediction markets, odds, or market prices were used. web_fetch failed because of provider configuration; the agent-reach web skill supplied readable source text for FIFA, Reuters and the Atlanta preview. Its web channel subsequently returned a rate-limit error, so further reads on that channel stopped; Le Monde, FIFPRO and El Doce evidence was verified through dated web_search results.
